title: 在绩效评估中谈成长：方向、实践机会和回顾时间
topic: 在绩效评估中谈成长：方向、实践机会和回顾时间

source.title: Making a Career — Your First Year
source.license: 原文按项目方确认的授权收录
source.context: 本课完整展示 37signals《Making a Career》中 Your First Year 小节。练习放在员工三个月评估之后：说明想发展的方向，提出具体的技能实践机会，并约定在六个月绩效评估时回顾。研究岗位与访谈项目为虚构练习，评估时间和发展反馈原则按手册原文。
paragraphs: Congratulations! You’re part of the team!

In your first few weeks, you’ll get aligned with your manager and team on approach and expectations. You’ll get up and running, doing real work. It’s your manager’s responsibility to give you proper opportunities to demonstrate your skills and fit for the job. This includes your technical expertise, your engagement with coworkers, and your ability to take feedback and adapt to the 37signals culture. Similarly, it’s on you to take advantage of those opportunities and to show that you’re capable of meeting the team standards.

When you start, you’ll receive an outline of expected performance metrics. Those standards will be clear and attainable, and your manager will give you frequent, candid feedback on how you’re doing meeting them, as you go.

You’ll have formal performance reviews with your manager at the 3-, 6-, and 12-month marks. On occasion, despite our collective best efforts, it’s not a fit. We don’t do full-scale performance improvement plans during the first year. So if during that time it starts looking like your long-term employment won’t work out, your manager will let you know early and why.

By the time you’ve reached your 1st anniversary with the company, we expect to be as excited about working with you as we were on day one. Likewise you should consider if you feel the same about having joined the team. When both of those answers are “hell yeah!”, you’ll move into a less frequent performance review cycle. Just once a year, around your anniversary of joining the company.

Your first year with 37signals should confirm what we learned in the hiring phase — you’re well suited for this job, and you’re invigorated by the work to be done. Just put in your best effort, make sure you reach out if things aren’t feeling right, embrace the feedback you get from your manager, and openly share your feedback with them!
translations: 恭喜！你已成为团队的一员！
在你最初的几周里，你将与经理和团队就工作方法和预期达成一致，并开始做实际工作。经理有责任给你适当的机会展示技能和岗位匹配度，包括专业能力、与同事的互动，以及接受反馈并适应 37signals 文化的能力。同样，你也应抓住机会，证明自己能够达到团队标准。
入职时，你会收到一份预期绩效指标概述。标准会清晰且可实现；经理会在工作过程中频繁、坦诚地反馈你达到这些标准的情况。
你会在入职第 3、6、12 个月时与经理进行正式绩效评估。有时尽管双方尽力，岗位仍可能不合适。第一年不会进行全面的绩效改进计划；如果长期雇佣关系可能无法继续，经理会尽早说明并解释原因。
工作满一周年时，公司希望仍像第一天那样期待与你共事；你也应考虑自己是否仍然很高兴加入团队。只有双方都非常愿意继续合作时，绩效评估才会改为低频安排：在入职周年前后每年一次。
37signals 的第一年应进一步确认招聘阶段的判断：你适合这份工作，也对接下来的工作充满动力。尽力做好本职；如果情况不对劲，要主动联系经理，接受经理的反馈，也坦诚分享你对经理的反馈。

fullChapterParagraphs: Congratulations! You’re part of the team!

In your first few weeks, you’ll get aligned with your manager and team on approach and expectations. You’ll get up and running, doing real work. It’s your manager’s responsibility to give you proper opportunities to demonstrate your skills and fit for the job. This includes your technical expertise, your engagement with coworkers, and your ability to take feedback and adapt to the 37signals culture. Similarly, it’s on you to take advantage of those opportunities and to show that you’re capable of meeting the team standards.

When you start, you’ll receive an outline of expected performance metrics. Those standards will be clear and attainable, and your manager will give you frequent, candid feedback on how you’re doing meeting them, as you go.

You’ll have formal performance reviews with your manager at the 3-, 6-, and 12-month marks. On occasion, despite our collective best efforts, it’s not a fit. We don’t do full-scale performance improvement plans during the first year. So if during that time it starts looking like your long-term employment won’t work out, your manager will let you know early and why.

By the time you’ve reached your 1st anniversary with the company, we expect to be as excited about working with you as we were on day one. Likewise you should consider if you feel the same about having joined the team. When both of those answers are “hell yeah!”, you’ll move into a less frequent performance review cycle. Just once a year, around your anniversary of joining the company.

Your first year with 37signals should confirm what we learned in the hiring phase — you’re well suited for this job, and you’re invigorated by the work to be done. Just put in your best effort, make sure you reach out if things aren’t feeling right, embrace the feedback you get from your manager, and openly share your feedback with them!

Advancing your career at 37signals doesn’t mean giving up on your craft. No matter your role, you can become better at the work itself and level up that way. This is especially important since we’re a relatively small company with few layers of managerial cake.

Within each of our job functions, we’ve mapped our trajectory of mastery to five different levels. That title structure is shared amongst all departments, but the particulars of what characterizes one level from another will of course be different.
Mid-level (L2)
Principal (L5)
Mastery and internal leveling are assessed and determined during hiring.

If you’re hired at a level below Senior, you should work towards developing Senior level skills. Juniors should achieve Senior in 4 years (2 to Mid-level, 2 to Senior), and Mid-level contributors should achieve Senior in 2 years. When everyone is able to follow that trajectory, we create healthy, high-performing teams where everyone can trust each other to run at similar speeds. When people aren’t able to level up within the above timeframes, after ample opportunities to do so, we usually determine that to be a bad long-term fit and we’ll decide to part ways.

Once you reach Senior, there is no expectation of further progression to Lead or Principal. In fact, most people will not achieve the Principal title! We see that level as reserved for people whose innovative work creates a resounding impact across the organization and even the industry. Those who do end up progressing all the way through our path usually have worked at 37signals for a decade or more.
The proficiencies expected of all of our major teams by level are documented here: Designers, Ops, Programmers, QA, and Support.

37signals pays at the top 10% for our industry at San Francisco salary levels, regardless of where you live. The comparison data is provided by a company called Radford that polls compensation data from all the major companies in our industry and plenty of our smaller peers as well.

Some jobs at 37signals are not matched to Radford comparison data. Compensation for common technical roles like programming and design is reliably competitive in a market like San Francisco. For some non-technical roles, compensation is much lower, and much less competitive. To compensate for that industry disparity, we instituted a $73,500 salary floor (floor adjusted for inflation since publishing).

The Radford data is reviewed once per year at the end of November. If it’s warranted, that is if the market rates in the top 10% have gone up, we’ll increase pay on January 1st to follow suit. We don’t decrease pay, even if the market rates may have dropped. If that happens, we’ll hold them steady until they come up again.
Everyone in the same role at the same level is paid the same at 37signals.
When you get a promotion, that is you move from one level to another, you’ll get a corresponding pay raise effective on your next pay cycle.

You’ll meet with your manager for formal performance reviews. When you’re new to 37signals, you’ll meet at the 3-month, 6-month, and 1-year marks. Then you’ll meet once a year, around your anniversary with the company. Your manager will share performance expectations for your role when you start, and they’ll keep you apprised of any changes to expectations should they evolve.
Managers are expected to document performance review outcomes and any action items or deadlines that come out of the meetings.

If your work performance is not meeting expectations, you may be put on a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP). We only initiate PIPs if your manager’s concern is correctable in the short term. We do not initiate PIPs for fundamental performance issues that relate to your core job skills. If you’re a Programmer whose coding skills are not at the level they need to be, we’d forego a PIP. However, we may initiate a PIP to help you improve your performance in a coachable skill like project management.

notes.phrase: proper opportunities to demonstrate your skills
notes.meaning: 适当的机会来展示你的技能
notes.explain: 来源把提供实践机会列为经理的责任；员工也要主动抓住机会并达到团队标准。
notes.example: Could I take on a task that gives me an opportunity to demonstrate my research skills?

notes.explain: feedback 会在工作过程中持续提供，不只发生在正式评估会上。
notes.example: I’d appreciate frequent, candid feedback as I build this skill.

notes.explain: 这是手册列出的第一年正式绩效评估节点。
notes.example: We can review my progress at my six-month performance review.

notes.phrase: move into a less frequent performance review cycle
notes.meaning: 转为频率较低的绩效评估周期
notes.explain: 只有公司和员工都愿意继续合作时，才会转为每年在入职周年前后评估一次；不是每季度评估。
notes.example: After the first year, performance reviews take place annually around the work anniversary.

scenario.title: Preparing for a three-month performance review
english: At a three-month review, an employee wants to grow into more customer-research work.
The manager is responsible for providing proper opportunities, and the employee should use them to demonstrate skills and learn from feedback.
The employee suggests joining the next customer-interview round to practice interviewing and asks to review progress at the six-month review.
chinese: 在入职三个月的评估中，一名员工希望逐步承担更多客户研究工作。
经理有责任提供合适的实践机会；员工也应抓住机会展示技能并从反馈中学习。
员工建议参加下一轮客户访谈来练习访谈技巧，并希望在六个月评估时回顾进展。

firstAttempt.prompt: 你在入职三个月的正式评估中，希望逐步承担更多客户研究工作。请用英文说明方向，提出参加下一轮客户访谈来练习访谈技能，并约定在六个月绩效评估时回顾进展。
firstAttempt.sample: I’d like to take on more customer research over time. Could I join the next round of customer interviews to build my interview skills? Could we review my progress at my six-month performance review?
firstAttempt.rationale: 先说发展方向，再提出能练习目标技能的真实工作机会，最后把回顾时间放到手册列出的六个月评估节点。

words.example: The next interview round would let me demonstrate my research skills.
words.translation: 下一轮访谈能让我展示研究技能。
words.note: 强调通过实际工作表现出能力。

words.example: I’d appreciate candid feedback on my interview notes.
words.translation: 我希望得到对访谈记录的坦诚反馈。
words.note: 常形容直接、诚实且有助改进的反馈。

words.example: Could you explain the performance metrics for my role?
words.translation: 你能说明一下我这个岗位的绩效指标吗？
words.note: 用于衡量岗位表现的标准；手册说这些标准应清楚且可实现。

words.example: Let’s review my progress at the six-month performance review.
words.translation: 我们在六个月绩效评估时回顾我的进展。
words.note: 手册列出第一年 3、6、12 个月的正式评估节点。

structure.original: Those standards will be clear and attainable, and your manager will give you frequent, candid feedback on how you’re doing meeting them, as you go.
analysis: Those standards will be clear and attainable 是并列形容词作表语，说明预期标准应清晰且可实现。
and 连接第二个分句；your manager 是主语，will give you 是“会给你”，frequent, candid feedback 是宾语。
on how you’re doing meeting them 说明反馈主题；as you go 表示工作推进过程中持续提供。
structure.transfer: Could I own the next onboarding guide update to practice clearer technical writing? Could we review the result at my six-month performance review?

rewrite.bad: I want to work in research. Give me something to do and let me know if I did well.
rewrite.good: I’d like to take on more customer research over time. Could I join the next round of customer interviews to build my interview skills? Could we review my progress at my six-month performance review?
rewrite.translation: 我希望逐步承担更多客户研究工作。我能否参加下一轮客户访谈来练习访谈技巧？我们能否在六个月绩效评估时回顾我的进展？
rewrite.pattern: I’d like to [grow in an area]. Could I [take on a task] to build my [skill]? Could we review my progress at [a stated review point]?

cloze.prompt: I’d like to take on more customer research over ___.
cloze.why: over time 表示逐步承担更多工作，而不是一次性换岗。

cloze.prompt: Could I join the interview round to build my interview ___?
cloze.why: build my interview skills 把具体实践任务与想培养的能力相连。

cloze.prompt: Could we review my progress at my six-month performance ___?
cloze.why: review 对应手册所列的六个月正式评估节点。

dictation.text: Your manager will give you frequent, candid feedback on how you’re doing meeting them, as you go.
dictation.label: 听写 1 · 工作中的坦诚反馈
dictation.why: 听辨 frequent, candid feedback 和 as you go 两个重点。

dictation.text: You’ll have formal performance reviews with your manager at the 3-, 6-, and 12-month marks.
dictation.label: 听写 2 · 第一年的评估节点
dictation.why: 听清 3、6、12 个月三个正式评估时间点。

apply.prompt: 你在三个月评估中想参加下一轮客户访谈练习。请说明发展方向、实践机会，并约定六个月时回顾。
apply.sample: I’d like to take on more customer research over time. Could I join the next round of customer interviews? Could we review my progress at my six-month performance review?

translationPractice.prompt: 我希望逐步承担更多客户研究工作。
translationPractice.answer: I’d like to take on more customer research over time.
translationPractice.why: take on more work over time 表达逐步增加相关职责的意愿。

translationPractice.prompt: 我能否参加下一轮客户访谈来练习访谈技巧？
translationPractice.answer: Could I join the next round of customer interviews to build my interview skills?
translationPractice.why: Could I ...? 礼貌地提出实践机会；to build 说明任务如何练习技能。

translationPractice.prompt: 我们能否在六个月绩效评估时回顾我的进展？
translationPractice.answer: Could we review my progress at my six-month performance review?
translationPractice.why: at my six-month performance review 明确约定回顾节点，并与手册时间表一致。

choice.prompt: 你在入职三个月的正式评估中，想逐步承担更多客户研究并练习访谈技能。请选择包含发展方向、具体实践机会和六个月回顾时间的表达。
options: I want a promotion. Please tell me when I will get one.
I’d like to take on more customer research over time. Could I join the next round of customer interviews to build my interview skills? Could we review my progress at my six-month performance review?
I’ll wait until the company assigns me a new role before asking for a development opportunity.
choice.why: 正确项说明发展方向、能展示技能的具体任务，以及手册列出的六个月评估回顾节点。

output.prompt: 在入职三个月评估中，你希望提高技术写作能力。请用英文提出负责下一次入职指南更新的机会，并约定在六个月绩效评估时讨论结果和下一步。
output.sample: I’d like to build my technical-writing skills by owning the next onboarding guide update. Could we review the result and discuss what I should practice next at my six-month performance review?
check: 是否提出了具体的工作实践机会？
是否把机会与要培养的技能联系起来？
是否约定在六个月评估时回顾结果和下一步？
